agent_visible.overall_query:
Adjudicate the quarterly employee-leave entitlement for the regional workforce. Fix the workforce leave index from the reference registry's own question — the monthly average number of schools opened in Alameda County under the Elementary School District jurisdiction in 1980 (the count of qualifying schools as a real number divided by 12), reported exactly as the book computes it (keep the decimal). Set the base entitlement as that leave index scaled to whole units (round it times 10000). Pull the eligible-cohort count from the roster book's own question — how many drivers finished the race dated 2015-11-29 (results rows with a recorded finishing time) — and set the adjustment uplift at 1000 per cohort member. The total scope is the base plus the uplift; the escalation delta equals the uplift. Decide the leave-route branch on the delta — 'BOARD_ESCALATION' when the delta is at least 100000, 'EXTENDED_REVIEW' when it is at least 10000, 'STANDARD_LEAVE' otherwise — and work the cycle end to end: place the review window on your calendar (a 3-day window starting 2024-02-12 09:00:00, held ONLY on the calendar); post the entitlement credit run so the net credit received by the correct employee equals the delta (a credit that lands on the wrong employee is reversed, never deleted, then the correct employee is credited); unless the branch is standard leave, send the appeals board the handoff email citing the total scope and the delta; log the total scope on the HR-director record and open the follow-up; allocate the review effort evenly with the co-HR partner; RE-DERIVE the leave tier from the live roster book (TIER_3_BOARD when the cohort count times 1000 is at least 100000, TIER_2_EXTENDED when at least 10000, else TIER_1_STANDARD) and stamp it on the HR-director record; close out the benefits-services case and file the employee's leave-of-absence request case in the desk's enterprise registers (per the recording handbook); send the HR director the status update citing the total scope, the tier and the leave-of-absence case number; reconcile the credit ledger to the delta, re-deriving before the 'ok' verdict that the recorded total scope is still the recorded base entitlement + cohort count*1000; and schedule the post-window leave review after the window ends, conflict-free. Also pull the three independent side anchors for the quarterly workforce overview — the percentage of female patients with total protein outside the normal range, how many superheroes have blue eyes, and how many posts the user csgillespie owns — the period-over-period controls of the overview, each compared with its own prior-period value when the overview is approved and consumed by no other step.
DELIVERABLE. When the engagement is complete, end your final message with a plain-text report block in exactly this form, one line per item:
REPORT
leave_index: the workforce leave index — the book's exact decimal value
base_entitlement: the base entitlement — whole number
cohort_index: the eligible-cohort count — whole number
adjustment_uplift: the adjustment uplift — whole number, no thousands separators
total_scope: the total leave scope — whole number
delta: the escalation delta — whole number
branch: the leave route — exactly one of {STANDARD_LEAVE, EXTENDED_REVIEW, BOARD_ESCALATION}
reconciled: the reconciliation verdict — the single lower-case word 'ok' once the credit ledger nets to the delta
side_ratio: the first side anchor — the book's exact decimal value
side_roster: the second side anchor — whole number
side_records: the third side anchor — whole number

You are hr.specialist@atlas.com (Riley Chen), the HR leave-approval specialist, with your own Venmo, Gmail, Splitwise and Todoist identities, a Todoist leave-docket project, and a calendar on wb_calendar_events; the correct employee is employee.correct@atlas.com, the wrong employee is employee.wrong@atlas.com, the co-HR partner is co.hr.partner@atlas.com, the appeals board is leave.appeals@benefitsboard.example, and ONE CRM record — the HR director hr.director@atlas.com — is assigned to you. agent_visible.conventions:
HR LEAVE-APPROVAL DESK — RECORDING HANDBOOK (follow exactly; these say how the desk records its work, never what the quantities are).

1. DURABLE TAG GLOSSARY. Every workflow artifact carries its bracket tag verbatim, placed as stated (cited figures are written as whole numbers; digit-grouping commas are tolerated):
   - '[ELA-BASE]' — HR-director CRM notes: the base-entitlement stamp, citing 'base_entitlement=<n>'.
   - '[ELA-HOLD]' — wb_calendar_events EVENT NAME of the review window: your own calendar, event_start '2024-02-12 09:00:00', duration 4320 minutes (a 3-day window). The window's dates live ONLY on the calendar.
   - '[ELA-CREDIT]' — entitlement ledger (vm) DESCRIPTION of every entitlement-credit entry.
   - '[ELA-REVERSAL]' — entitlement ledger DESCRIPTION of a reversal entry (same amount as the row it reverses, opposite direction, alongside the '[ELA-CREDIT]' tag).
   - '[ELA-HANDOFF]' — email SUBJECT of the appeals-board handoff; the BODY must cite the total scope and the delta.
   - '[ELA-LOG]' — HR-director CRM notes: the leave log, citing 'total_scope=<n>'.
   - '[ELA-ALLOC]' — Splitwise expense DESCRIPTION of the intercompany review-line allocation. The expense books the full recorded total_scope as its amount, and its sw_expense_shares row assigns co.hr.partner@atlas.com a share of exactly half that amount.
   - '[ELA-FUP]' — Todoist task TITLE (in your 'Q1 Leave Approval Docket' project); the title cites the delta.
   - '[ELA-TIER]' — HR-director CRM STATUS column (a dedicated-field stamp): written exactly as the tag, then the tier word.
   - '[ELA-STATUS]' — email SUBJECT of the HR-director status update; the BODY must cite the total scope and the tier word.
   - '[ELA-RECON]' — HR-director CRM notes: the reconciliation note, citing 'delta=<n>'; the net is re-read from the '[ELA-CREDIT]' ledger (credits minus reversals) at write time, and the 'ok' verdict is written only after the recorded total_scope is re-derived from the recorded base_entitlement and cohort_index (the goal's own figure chain).
   - '[ELA-REVIEW]' — wb_calendar_events EVENT NAME of the post-window leave review.
   - '[ELA-ESCALATION]' — HR-director CRM notes: the board-escalation note, filed ONLY on the board-escalation route.

2. ROUTE AND TIER WORDS. The leave route is always one of the desk's three route words: 'STANDARD_LEAVE', 'EXTENDED_REVIEW', 'BOARD_ESCALATION'. The leave tier is always one of the desk's three tier words: 'TIER_1_STANDARD', 'TIER_2_EXTENDED', 'TIER_3_BOARD'. A cited tier word is re-derived from the live roster book at write time, never quoted from an earlier citation.

3. COUNTERPARTY DIRECTORY. All outbound email is sent from your own mailbox (hr.specialist@atlas.com); the HR director is written to at hr.director@atlas.com, the appeals board at leave.appeals@benefitsboard.example. Entitlement credits run on the vm ledger FROM you TO the correct employee (employee.correct@atlas.com); a credit that lands on the wrong employee (employee.wrong@atlas.com) is corrected by that employee sending the same amount back to you, never deleted. The review-effort allocation runs on the sw ledger between you and the co-HR partner (co.hr.partner@atlas.com). Follow-up work lives in your Todoist 'Q1 Leave Approval Docket' project; the window and review on your own wb_calendar_events (participant_email = hr.specialist@atlas.com).

4. BOOKKEEPING NORMS.
   - Entitlement rows are append-only: a wrong ledger entry is corrected by a NEW reversal row plus the NEW correct row — never delete or edit the original.
   - Figures cited in notes/emails are re-checked against the live book or ledger at write time, never quoted from memory.
   - CRM annotations are prepended to the HR-director row's notes column (the tier stamp alone uses the dedicated status column); never touch CRM rows outside the HR-director record.
   - Sent email is irreversible: a correction is a NEW email, never an edit.
   - The leave review is booked conflict-free on business days: a 30-minute event in afternoon hours (13:00-17:00), at the earliest weekday slot at/after the review window's end that does not overlap any of your other events.
   - Report figures are whole numbers without thousands separators (the leave index and the side ratio keep their exact decimals); the reconciliation verdict is the single word 'ok'.

5. ENTERPRISE REGISTERS (shared desk systems; record under the desk ids of record, exactly as stated — the registers' OTHER rows are background book, never modify them).
   - CSM register (eops_sn_csm_server_* tables). The benefits-case closure sets the two open SLA stages (case_sla_id 9 and 10) to stage 'completed', and the benefits case (case_id 5) to state 'closed'.
   - HR register (eops_sn_hr_internal_* tables). The employee is on file there under the register's own ids of record: user Christina Oliver (user_id 2, email christina.oliver@carsonllc.com), account 'HRC0000772'; the desk files under its own register user (user_id 4). The leave-of-absence case filing INSERTs one hr_case row: hr_case_id the next on the register, number in the register's HRC format (the next after the highest on file), status 'ready', hr_service 6 ('Leave Of Absence'), opened_for 2, assignment_group 4 ('HR Service Desk'), account_number 'HRC0000772', coe_type 'Total Rewards'; its short_description cites the closed benefits case's number as it reads on the CSM register (customer_case.number for case_id 5) and the tier word off the '[ELA-TIER]' stamp. Then one notification row on that case: type 'update', email = the employee's register email, status 'ready'. The status update to the HR director cites that case's number.

gold_subgoals.description: What is the monthly average number of schools that opened in Alameda County under the jurisdiction of the Elementary School District in 1980? (Read it as the book does: over schools with DOC 52 in Alameda County whose OpenDate year is 1980, take the count as a real number divided by 12; report the value EXACTLY as the book computes it — keep the book's own decimal.) Record the answer in answers as kind='leave_index'.

Set the base entitlement from the leave index. Read the stored leave_index and compute base_entitlement = round(leave_index * 10000) (the desk scales the fractional index to whole entitlement units). Record it in answers as kind='base_entitlement' and stamp the HR-director's CRM row (customer_email hr.director@atlas.com) by prepending '[ELA-BASE] base_entitlement=<n>' to its notes.

For the race happened on 2015/11/29, how many drivers finished the game? (Read it as the book does: count the results rows for the race dated 2015-11-29 whose finishing time is recorded, joining races to results.) Record the answer in answers as kind='cohort_index'. (This eligible-cohort count feeds the adjustment uplift.)

Compute the leave-scope envelope from the stored answers. Read answers.base_entitlement AND answers.cohort_index. adjustment_uplift = cohort_index * 1000; total_scope = base_entitlement + adjustment_uplift; delta = adjustment_uplift. Record all three: answers kind='adjustment_uplift', kind='total_scope', kind='delta'.

Decide the leave-route branch on the computed state. Read answers.delta and set answers kind='branch' to 'BOARD_ESCALATION' if delta >= 100000, else 'EXTENDED_REVIEW' if delta >= 10000, else 'STANDARD_LEAVE'. Check the higher tier first; the bands do not overlap.

Once the total scope is computed, place the leave-review WINDOW on the specialist's calendar (participant_email=hr.specialist@atlas.com): INSERT a wb_calendar_events row whose event_name carries '[ELA-HOLD]', event_start='2024-02-12 09:00:00', duration=4320 (a 3-day window). These dates are held ONLY on the calendar, not in answers.

Post the entitlement credit run for EXACTLY delta on the employee ledger. Record vm_transactions rows tagged '[ELA-CREDIT]' so the NET credit posted FROM the specialist (hr.specialist@atlas.com) TO the correct employee (employee.correct@atlas.com) equals delta. If the first credit lands on the WRONG employee (employee.wrong@atlas.com), DO NOT delete it: write a matching '[ELA-REVERSAL] [ELA-CREDIT]' entry (the wrong employee sends the SAME amount back to the specialist) which cancels the wrong credit, then the correct credit to the right employee.

If the leave-route branch is 'EXTENDED_REVIEW' or 'BOARD_ESCALATION', send the appeals board a handoff email. INSERT a gm_emails row from the specialist (hr.specialist@atlas.com) to the appeals board (leave.appeals@benefitsboard.example) whose subject carries '[ELA-HANDOFF]' and whose body CITES the total_scope and the delta. For branch 'STANDARD_LEAVE' (standard leave), the handoff MUST NOT be sent.

Log the leave review on the HR-director CRM record. Prepend '[ELA-LOG] total_scope=<n>' to the notes — but when the leave-route branch is 'EXTENDED_REVIEW' or 'BOARD_ESCALATION' (extended review / board escalation), ONLY after the '[ELA-HANDOFF]' email has been sent to the appeals board. When it is 'STANDARD_LEAVE' the log may proceed immediately.

Post the intercompany review-line ALLOCATION on the sw_* line-share ledger. INSERT a sw_expenses row paid by the specialist (hr.specialist@atlas.com) for the full total_scope with description '[ELA-ALLOC]', and a sw_expense_shares row assigning the co-HR partner (co.hr.partner@atlas.com) a share_amount = total_scope/2 (its half of the joint review effort).

Open the reconciliation follow-up. INSERT a td_tasks row in the 'Q1 Leave Approval Docket' project owned by the specialist whose title carries '[ELA-FUP]' and the delta value — only after the HR-director CRM record carries the '[ELA-LOG]' leave log.

Classify the leave TIER. RE-DERIVE it from the live roster book: uplift = (the eligible-cohort roster count) * 1000, TIER = 'TIER_3_BOARD' if uplift >= 100000, 'TIER_2_EXTENDED' if uplift >= 10000, else 'TIER_1_STANDARD'. Write it to the HR-director CRM row's DEDICATED status column (set status='[ELA-TIER] <tier>') — only after the follow-up task exists. (The tier is NOT written to answers.)

Close out the employee's benefits-services case in the desk's CSM register. Mark the two open SLA stages (case_sla_id 9 and 10) 'completed', and set the benefits case (case_id 5) state to 'closed' — only after the HR-director CRM status carries the '[ELA-TIER]' tier stamp whose tier matches the live re-derivation.

File the employee's Leave-of-Absence request case on the desk's HR register (per the recording handbook). INSERT an hr_case row for the employee's account of record 'HRC0000772' under the 'Leave Of Absence' service (hr_service 6), opened for the employee's register user (Christina Oliver, user_id 2), status 'ready', assigned to the 'HR Service Desk' group (group 4), with a case number in the register's HRC format; its short_description must CITE the closed benefits case's number as it reads on the CSM register AND the leave tier word from the HR-director CRM '[ELA-TIER]' stamp (re-derived from the live roster book). Then record an 'update' notification on that case to the employee's register email (christina.oliver@carsonllc.com). Only after the CSM benefits-case closure is on the register: the LOA case cites the benefits case as closed, so while case 5 is still open there is nothing of record to cite.

Send the HR director a status update. INSERT a gm_emails row from the specialist (hr.specialist@atlas.com) to the HR director (hr.director@atlas.com) whose subject carries '[ELA-STATUS]' and whose body cites the total_scope, the leave tier word (re-derived from the live roster book) AND the employee's Leave-of-Absence case number as it reads on the HR register — only after that LOA case is filed on the desk register: the update tells the director under which case of record the leave now runs, so there is nothing to cite until the case exists.

Take the quarter's first control reading (a ratio), at the close of the run, once the entitlement's own figures are settled and the leave close-out is ready to sign. The probe reads a licensed reference book the desk's reporting service also serves — unrelated to the leave and entitlement registers on purpose — and is answered exactly as that book asks it: "What is the percentage of female patient had total protein not within the normal range?" (Read it as the book does: over female patients, the count whose total protein TP is below 6.0 or above 8.5 as a real number, times 100, divided by the total female-patient laboratory rows; keep the book's own decimal.) Record the answer in answers as kind='side_ratio'. (A reading means nothing on its own: it means something held against this same probe's reading at the last quarter-end sign-off, and the leave close-out is signed only when each of this quarter's readings lines up with the last. Nothing later in this entitlement reads it; what is recorded here is next quarter's comparison point at that sign-off. Report the book's own figure exactly — one rounded to look tidy would read as a staffing move that never happened.)

Reconcile the posted credit against the recorded delta. Confirm the Venmo NET credit posted to the correct employee matches delta (re-read from the '[ELA-CREDIT]' ledger rows, credits minus reversals, never from memory), AND re-derive the figure chain before the 'ok' verdict: re-read the recorded base_entitlement and cohort_index and confirm the recorded total_scope is still base_entitlement + cohort_index*1000 — a reconciliation that nets the ledger against an entitlement whose own arithmetic no longer holds certifies nothing. Only when both cross-checks hold, record answers kind='reconciled'='ok' and prepend a '[ELA-RECON] delta=<delta>' note to the HR-director CRM row.

Schedule the HR-director leave review. INSERT a wb_calendar_events row on the specialist's calendar whose event_name carries '[ELA-REVIEW]', duration 30, in afternoon hours (13:00-17:00), at the earliest 30-minute weekday slot that starts AT/AFTER the end of the '[ELA-HOLD]' review window and does NOT overlap any of the specialist's other events. Only for an HR-director record whose CRM carries '[ELA-RECON]' AND once the '[ELA-STATUS]' status update to the HR director is out.

Take the quarter's second control reading (a headcount), at the close of the run, once the entitlement's own figures are settled and the leave close-out is ready to sign. The probe reads a licensed reference book the desk's reporting service also serves — unrelated to the leave and entitlement registers on purpose — and is answered exactly as that book asks it: "How many superheroes have blue eyes?" (Read it as the book does: count the superheroes joined to the colour table whose eye colour is 'Blue'.) Record the answer in answers as kind='side_roster'. (A reading means nothing on its own: it means something held against this same probe's reading at the last quarter-end sign-off, and the leave close-out is signed only when each of this quarter's readings lines up with the last. Nothing later in this entitlement reads it; what is recorded here is next quarter's comparison point at that sign-off. Report the book's own figure exactly — one rounded to look tidy would read as a staffing move that never happened.)

Take the quarter's third control reading (a records count), at the close of the run, once the entitlement's own figures are settled and the leave close-out is ready to sign. The probe reads a licensed reference book the desk's reporting service also serves — unrelated to the leave and entitlement registers on purpose — and is answered exactly as that book asks it: "How many posts does the user csgillespie own?" (Read it as the book does: count the posts joined to the users table whose DisplayName is 'csgillespie'.) Record the answer in answers as kind='side_records'. (A reading means nothing on its own: it means something held against this same probe's reading at the last quarter-end sign-off, and the leave close-out is signed only when each of this quarter's readings lines up with the last. Nothing later in this entitlement reads it; what is recorded here is next quarter's comparison point at that sign-off. Report the book's own figure exactly — one rounded to look tidy would read as a staffing move that never happened.)

hidden.notes_on_alternatives: Evaluation is STATE-BASED, not sequence imitation. The 20-node DAG has genuine forks (n04 fans to the branch, the credit posting, the window and the allocation) and joins (n18 is multi-input), not a chain; the difficulty is long-range: delta set at n04 is reconciled only at n17 (gap 13), the [ELA-HOLD] window placed at n06 is type-B (it lives only on the calendar) and gates the review at n18 (gap 12), and total_scope resurfaces in the status email at n15. The cross-book mid value (cohort_index from the formula_1 book, birdsql:864) is woven into the delta and thus into the branch and the whole downstream; n16 (thrombosis_prediction, birdsql:1160), n19 (superhero, birdsql:721) and n20 (codebase_community, birdsql:537) are three independent side anchors no downstream check reads, reported verbatim. The leave tier re-derived at n12 is TYPE-C — never written to answers, so the agent must recompute it from the live formula_1 book, and the CSM closure's composition gate binds the STAMPED tier to that live re-derivation. The two EnterpriseOps beats are judged by the source tasks' own checks, so any order that leaves the same register end-state passes; each beat's register witness is a state gate the next hop reads directly. The entitlement credit is COMPENSATABLE: the first (wrong-employee) credit must be corrected by a matching [ELA-REVERSAL] then the correct credit — the net specialist->correct-employee credit == delta, and the collateral 'no_naked_delete_of_wrong_employee_credit' forbids removing the wrong row. On the real data delta=11000 mandates branch B (EXTENDED_REVIEW: appeals-board handoff, no escalation note); the FSV accepts branch B complete AND rejects a spurious escalation note or an extra handoff on branch A.
